title: Re-implement plyr::eval.quoted, plyr::as.quoted
description:
As with the others, it's not 100% clear there's a lot of value (besides maybe the new tests) in this PR at the moment. But since it's done, I'm sharing it anyway.

Written by Gemini.

This completes the series -- {plyr} is no longer required by package code.

It _is_ still required by examples using `plyr::.`. So that would technically mean moving {plyr} to Suggests without further work (e.g. to re-implement `.` as a `reshape2` export). Eschewing that for now.

https://github.com/hadley/reshape/blob/03373426695f28edbf2a542fa43353dbdab3c4a6/man/cast.Rd#L94-L96

If you're keen to adopt any subset of these changes, I can help by putting them in a [`jj`](https://github.com/jj-vcs/jj) stack that will facilitate merging without having to deal with so many merge conflicts among them. Let me know.

title: Use testthat 3rd edition
description:
Made this update on our fork so figured I'd pass along the changes here too.

Some context: for a long time internally we had no concept of "Imports", only "Suggests"/"Depends" existed; we're trying to fix that now but there's an Everest of tech debt behind that.

When I tried to make the switch to testthat's Imports, reshape2's tests broke (internally) because `library(reshape2)` loads 'magrittr' after 'testthat' (for the moment, at least) and this suite uses `equals()` which resolves to `magrittr::equals()` (again, internally).

To be clear this suite is definitely WAI and the breakage is completely an internal thing, but still gives us a nice motivation to update the test style.

Happy to apply further edits as needed for style.

Also feel free to close if you'd rather not make the change.

title: Use explicit imports from plyr

In another ideal we'd also do away with {reshape2}, but the dependency footprint thereof is much less manageable, for now.

For now, a step towards removing {plyr} is identifying exactly how {reshape2} uses it.

title: Handle special attributes
description:
Currently `melt_dataframe()` creates names attributes that aren't necessarily the same length as the output vector, which makes the print method crash.

``` r
# Can only create named column vectors with dplyr
df <- dplyr::data_frame(col1 = c(a = 1, b = 2), col2 = c(a = 10, b = 20))
df <- tidyr::gather(df, "col", "value")

str(df$value)
## [1] "numeric"
##  Named num [1:4] 1 2 10 20
##  - attr(*, "names")= chr [1:2] "a" "b"

print(df$value)
##  *** caught segfault ***
## address 0x400000ae, cause 'memory not mapped'
##
## Traceback:
##  1: print.default(df$value)
##  2: print(df$value)
##
## Possible actions:
## 1: abort (with core dump, if enabled)
## 2: normal R exit
## 3: exit R without saving workspace
## 4: exit R saving workspace
## Selection:
```

This fix concatenates the names of the melted vectors so that the output is appropriately named.

It also takes care of `dim` and `dimnames` because `melt_dataframe()` uses `SET_ATTRIB` wihch bypasses the sanity checks that are normally triggered when modifying those attributes from R, and thus also break various consistency assumptions. These attributes are now simply discarded.

title: Allow value to be factor when dcast
description:
# Bug

When the value from a `melt` is a factor, attempting to `dcast` it into a form with multiple columns threw an error
# Reproducible code

``` r
df <- data.frame(fac1 = letters[1:4], fac2 = LETTERS[1:4], x = factor(1:4))
mx <- melt(df, id = c("fac1", "fac2"), measure.var = "x")
c2 <- dcast(mx, fac1 ~ fac2 + variable)
```
# Produced output

``` r
Error in names(data) <- array_names(res$labels[[2]]) : 
  'names' attribute [4] must be the same length as the vector [1]
```
# Problem

In `dcast`, (part of) the results from (the internal) `cast` are passed to `as.data.frame`.  This part is created by directly adding a `dim` attribute to the structure of the ordered data.  When this is added to a factor, it creates a factor with dimensions, but one that does not have class matrix.  Rather, it has class factor.  Thus when `as.data.frame` is called on it, it actually creates an invalid data.frame. (This may be a separate bug in 
`as.data.frame.factor` which assumes that the factor does not have a `dim` attribute.)
# Solution

Rather than allow `as.data.frame` to dispatch, call `as.data.frame.matrix` explicitly.  This is reasonable since we are expecting a matrix shape.

title: melt gets names from tables (fixes #14)
description:
After posting to the mailing list, I saw that this bug (#14) was already reported. 

This change needs to be roxygenized to take effect. I didn't do it here because it modified some of the .Rd files. (I installed roxygen2 from CRAN -- maybe I have a different version?)

After the change, these two melt commands should give the same output:

``` R
m <- matrix(101:106, nrow=2, dimnames=list(therows=1:2, thecols=1:3))

melt(m)
melt(as.table(m))
```

title: Make melt to preserve classes of measure variables when they are all the same.
description:
I guess the most common usage case for melt is when all columns have the same class. 

Currently melt downgrades classes. For example

```
   df <- data.frame(id = 1:2, date1 = Sys.Date(), date2 = Sys.Date() + 10)
   melt(df, measure.vars=c("date1", "date2"))
```

gives

```
     id variable value
   1  1    date1 15539
   2  2    date1 15539
   3  1    date2 15549
   4  2    date2 15549
```

With this patch it produces:

```
     id variable      value
   1  1    date1 2012-07-18
   2  2    date1 2012-07-18
   3  1    date2 2012-07-28
   4  2    date2 2012-07-28
```

title: Avoid using memcpy on STRSXPs
description:
As per correspondence with Matt Dowle, SET_STRING_ELT ensures that
objects are properly aged (see CHECK_OLD_TO_NEW in SET_STRING_ELT,
in memory.c). If we just use memcpy, because CHARSXPs are SEXPs,
there is a chance they will be gc'ed if R needs to shrink the
global string cache, and a raw memcpy won't properly protect them
from the gc.

title: Informative message if no id.vars
description:
Sometimes there is a need to melt data "as is", i.e. with no arguments provided:

``` r
df <- data.frame(a=1:3, b=4:6)
melt(df)
```

The output is 

``` r
Using  as id variables
  variable value
1        a     1
2        a     2
3        a     3
4        b     4
5        b     5
6        b     6
```

The message is not very informative and may be misleading. A small "if" handles this case, changing the message.
